steps.title: Reject an unsigned non-executable bundle before native launch
preconditions: Run the existing public CLI tooling journey on macOS through tracer app -- test tooling.
The journey creates an external synthetic Unsigned.app with one regular Contents/MacOS/Scriv file, mode 0600, so the fixture cannot execute. No supplied real app is used.
This catalog witnesses the unsigned prelaunch failure and its safe evidence only. Root must separately verify valid real signed/ad-hoc bundles, postrun checks and post-export failure handling.

expectations.description: The unsigned fixture exits with code 2 before any native scenario starts, emits no stderr or private signing output, records the safe app-signature-verification-failed blocker with not-run status and null app identity, preserves unknown source-to-app matching and both completion flags false, and leaves synthetic fixture bytes unchanged.

mappings.why: The Darwin platform verifier rejects the unsigned non-executable synthetic bundle before file fingerprinting or scenario execution. This test asserts rejection, not valid signing, all-architecture behavior or native acceptance.

Initial identity handling preserves the fixed signature-verification failure instead of converting it into the generic identity blocker. The evidence remains null app identity because assignment never completes.

The safe blocker path records the signature failure as not-run and assigns it to the unstarted workspace scenario. Other allowlisted blockers and started-scenario failure behavior remain outside this new negative assertion.

scenarios.title: Safe public CLI signature rejection before native scenario launch
